inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The Liberal Party is fracturing from within as MPs push for a leadership rethink, but the real story is how the opposition leader and figures like Angus Taylor are digging in to block even modest steps toward fairness. Angus Taylor has flatly rejected Andrew Hastie's call for the party to be “open-minded” about raising taxes on gas companies and ending concessions that benefit property investors. This clash makes it obvious the current leadership is doubling down on shielding corporate profits and the advantages held by wealthy investors instead of delivering the structural changes needed to reduce inequality and protect vulnerable groups. The leader also refused to back Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump and would not say if they support the US and Israel’s war with Iran.
